result.reasoning:
The premise is factually true but the consequence is false: the two published numbers are exactly the numbers the production reward sees, and the published labels already describe the sign-flipped books, so no number and no conclusion changes.

1. Premise confirmed, consequence not. s2 really has no sign lock (`sign_locked` key absent in every runs/F1*/sweep_s2.json; seg_hiliq_p sign=-1 in 15/15, seg_new_p -1 in 14/15 — F111 is +1), and s3 locks them all to +1. But the lock added at /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/scripts/sweep.py:142 is the ONLY sign lock in the repo (grep over partura/ and scripts/). The reward that actually drives the search, /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/partura/steer.py:426, does `for sign in (1.0, -1.0)` and keeps the best "(direction, half-life) BY THE LONG BOOK on train". So the "现在的方向约定" the finding appeals to does not exist in the reward: direction is maximized over, not locked to +1.

2. Reproduced: the published s2 row IS the reward-convention row. s2 and s3 are the same data (splits, expression and v_base/k_known utrain Sharpes bit-identical for all 15 factors), so they are simply the two directions of the same panel. Picking per factor the direction with the higher train long Sharpe (what steer.reward keeps) and then scoring on utrain reproduces the published row digit for digit:
   seg_hiliq_p  d_median +1.01, up 87%, down 7%, both 93%  (= the 3.1 table row; s3-locked row is -3.18/0%/100%)
   seg_new_p    d_median +0.41, up 60%, down 13%, both 27% (= the 3.1 table row; s3-locked row is -4.47/0%/100%)
   The s2 direction beats the locked +1 direction on the train long book in 14/15 factors for both ids. The s3 numbers are the LOSING direction, which the reward would never keep.

3. The label is right, not reversed. I ran the real operator: `cs_first_high40(y,x) = rank(y) + 1[rank(x)>0.6]`, so negating it puts the whole high-turnover 40% below everything else; `-1 * cs_first_high40(X, LIQ)` is per-day order-IDENTICAL to `cs_last_high40(neg(X), LIQ)` (verified exactly), and its top decile is 0% drawn from the high-40% turnover segment (100% for the locked +1 version). That is precisely the published label "把成交额最高四成排到最后" (scripts/guidance_report.py:91) — note sweep.py's own `why` string for the same id says the opposite ("只在成交额最高 40% 里选"), i.e. the report author deliberately relabeled to the measured book. The sign-flipped screen is therefore NOT silently mis-scored here.

4. Conclusion 1 / R2 / U5 are untouched. motif_stats rows are byte-identical between s2 and s3 for seg_lowliq_m (+1.18/87%/7%/93%), seg_lowliq_p, seg_xfrozen_m and scr_xhi_p — their rank IC sign was already +1. The +1.2 / "13 of 15" / "14 of 15" figures quoted in conclusion 1 and in guidance/B01.yaml R2's `why` all come from seg_lowliq_m, so they do not move at all. And the economic claim is identical under either reading: s2 says "pushing the high-liquidity 40% to the bottom buys +1.01", s3 says "being forced to pick inside the high-liquidity 40% costs -3.18" — both say the long-leg money is the low-liquidity tilt, which is exactly what R2 asserts.

5. No generator-facing prior is wrong. guidance/motif_stats_<tag>.json is read only by scripts/guidance_report.py (the human report); the machine-readable priors are guidance/B01.yaml, where `cs_first_high40` appears in no pattern at all, and U5 (line 127) already weights `{cs_last_high20|cs_last_high40|cs_first_low40}(_, _)` — i.e. the very structure the s2 book is order-identical to, with evidence drawn from seg_lowliq_m (unchanged). The hypothesised harm ("生成器…拿到的是本批最差的一类候选") needs both a rule that does not exist and a locked-sign reward that does not exist.

6. The suggested fix would make things worse, and its rename is itself wrong by a sign. Citing only s3 would replace the better-direction measurement with the losing one, and under the lock sweep.py generates no `cs_last_*(·, LIQ)` complement at all (only cs_first_high40 with X and neg(X), both of which keep the high-liq 40% on top), so the "push the high-liq names to the bottom" book would disappear from the evidence base entirely. The proposed rename `cs_last_high40(X, LIQ)` is not the measured book: the measured one is `cs_last_high40(neg(X), LIQ)` (I verified `cs_last_high40(X, LIQ)` has a different per-day ordering).

Only residue, which changes no published number: regenerating the report with `--tag s3` would make the two NAMES labels wrong, and the seg_new_p s2 row pools 14 "newest 40% to the bottom" books with F111's one opposite-direction book (dropping F111 leaves the median at +0.40 vs the published +0.41, so it is immaterial).

Scripts: /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/review/verify/refute_s2_sign/semantics.py and crosstag.py. No existing file was modified.

result.corrected_fix:
No change to research/alpha_distillation/B01_reverse_guidance.md or guidance/B01.yaml is warranted: both 3.1 rows equal the value the reward (partura/steer.py:426, best of the two directions by the train long book) would see, the labels already describe the measured books, and the s2/s3 readings support conclusion 1 / R2 identically.

If anything is worth doing, it is two small, number-preserving items:
1. scripts/sweep.py variants(): under the sign lock the complement book is no longer generated for the hiliq / new families, so add it explicitly alongside the existing cs_first_* variants, e.g. `cs_last_high40({sg}, LIQ)` and `cs_last_low40({sg}, AGE)` for sg in (X, neg(X)). Then a locked run measures both "only pick inside the segment" and "push the segment to the bottom" instead of losing the latter.
2. scripts/guidance_report.py:91 NAMES: make the label tag-aware (or state the measured sign), because the current wording "把成交额最高四成排到最后" / "把上市最短的四成排到最后" is correct for the s2 (sign -1) books but becomes wrong if the report is ever regenerated with --tag s3, where those rows measure "只在成交额最高四成里选" / "只在上市最短的四成里选".

Do NOT adopt the finding's rename to `cs_last_high40(X, LIQ)`: the s2-measured book is order-identical to `cs_last_high40(neg(X), LIQ)`, not to the X version.
